description: University student interested in agriculture, climate science, and mathematics. Interested in building a tool that can benefit farmers to increase crop yields and efficiency.
summary:
Our project, fallo, is an agricultural decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotations adapted to changing environmental conditions. It combines 20 years of historical climate data from NASA POWER, soil information from USDA SSURGO surveys or regional reference profiles, crop characteristics, and farmer-selected priorities to generate and compare three-year crop rotation plans using Gemini-powered Super Intelligence (SI).

fallo also allows farmers to explore hypothetical changes in temperature and rainfall through its What-If Simulator, examine planting and harvesting periods with its Field Calendar, and identify historically similar growing seasons through Climate Analogues. Its recommendations are supported by deterministic agronomic validation and scoring, helping users understand the trade-offs between different strategies.

As climate variability, water stress, and soil degradation create growing challenges for agriculture, farmers need accessible ways to evaluate their options. fallo brings environmental data and crop-rotation planning together in one platform, helping farmers explore strategies for greater agricultural resilience while keeping local expertise and farmer judgment central to the decision-making process.
details:
fallo is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers explore crop rotations that are better adapted to their environmental conditions and farming priorities.

Users begin by creating a field and examining its 20-year climate history, including temperature, precipitation, and growing-season patterns. fallo retrieves climate information from NASA POWER and combines it with soil properties from USDA SSURGO surveys in the United States or regional soil reference profiles elsewhere. It also incorporates crop characteristics such as water demand, drought tolerance, nitrogen-fixing potential, and growing windows.

Using this information and farmer-selected priorities, Gemini-powered Super Intelligence (SI) helps generate three-year crop rotation proposals. Deterministic agronomic validation and a multi-factor scoring system support comparisons between strategies. Farmers can then use the What-If Simulator to explore hypothetical temperature and rainfall changes, the Field Calendar to examine planting and harvesting windows, and Climate Analogues to identify historically similar growing seasons.

We developed fallo using TypeScript, React, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS, with Google Gemini Enterprise providing SI-assisted generation. Its environmental data integrations include NASA POWER and USDA soil data services, while custom algorithms handle climate analysis, scenario simulation, rotation scoring, and historical comparisons. The application uses interactive charts and visualizations to make complex information accessible.

What makes fallo creative is its integration of historical Earth observation data, soil information, SI-assisted reasoning, and deterministic agronomic logic into one connected planning workflow. Rather than presenting a single recommendation, it allows farmers to compare strategies, adjust their priorities, and investigate how changing environmental conditions could affect their choices.

We considered climate variability, soil health, water availability, crop suitability, growing seasons, crop diversity, and individual farmer priorities. Our intended impact is to help farmers make more informed decisions, explore potentially more resilient rotations, and better prepare for changing agricultural conditions, ultimately supporting the sector that is essential for feeding and sustaining a growing global population.
